description: REQ-109's cross-feature composition of `excludeDefaultedBorrowers` into `anicca-agent-spawn`'s own colony-wide surplus pipeline has a disproportionate, unbounded, unstated blast radius that the spec never quantifies, caps, or reconciles against that sibling feature's own semantics. REQ-109 (lines 1022-1030) states: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL ALSO exclude that borrower from any colony-wide surplus/eligible-citizen aggregation this codebase performs (today: `anicca-agent-spawn`'s `computeColonySurplusUsd`/`filterProductiveCitizens`) -- realized via a SECOND, lending-owned filter pass, `excludeDefaultedBorrowers({citizens, loanRows}) -> citizens[]` ... composed AFTER `filterProductiveCitizens`'s own output and BEFORE `computeColonySurplusUsd` runs.' Re-read this session, `anicca-agent-spawn`'s own CURRENT `specs/behavioral-spec.md` (REQ-101, lines 262-267) confirms `computeColonySurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd})` runs ONLY on `filterProductiveCitizens`'s output, summing EACH remaining citizen's own `max(0, balance_i - perCitizenReserveUsd)` -- meaning `excludeDefaultedBorrowers` removing a citizen record ENTIRELY from that array causes that citizen's WHOLE current balance (not merely the defaulted debt amount, which per REQ-104 can be as small as `$0.022`) to contribute `0` to colony-wide spawn-eligibility surplus computation, indefinitely, since REQ-109's own edge cases (lines 1045-1049) explicitly state 'no future increment ever adds a write-off mechanism' this increment. A citizen could default on the smallest possible loan in this system ($0.02 principal) and, as a structural consequence never stated or justified anywhere in this spec, have its ENTIRE balance -- however large it later becomes through unrelated gig-work or trading -- permanently excluded from `anicca-agent-spawn`'s own spawn-decision arithmetic (REQ-102/`decideColonySpawn` in that sibling spec, which consumes `computeColonySurplusUsd`'s output), with no proportionality to the actual defaulted amount, no time bound, and no acknowledgment that this is even a consequence for a DIFFERENT feature's decision-making, not merely this feature's own lending/eligibility scope. This is a real, load-bearing side effect of the composition this spec chooses, and it is never quantified, capped, or reconciled against `anicca-agent-spawn`'s own REQ-102 spawn-eligibility requirements -- which this feature explicitly commits (REQ-113) to never modify or directly couple to, yet this composition point does exactly that, functionally.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL ALSO exclude that borrower from any colony-wide surplus/eligible-citizen aggregation this codebase performs (today: anicca-agent-spawn's computeColonySurplusUsd/filterProductiveCitizens) -- realized via a SECOND, lending-owned filter pass, excludeDefaultedBorrowers({citizens, loanRows}) -> citizens[] ... composed AFTER filterProductiveCitizens's own output and BEFORE computeColonySurplusUsd runs.

crossCheck.note: computeColonySurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd}) then runs ONLY on filterProductiveCitizens's OUTPUT -- never on the raw registry array -- where balance_i is that citizen's own most-recently-read liquid balance ... This confirms excludeDefaultedBorrowers's removal of a citizen record has a whole-balance effect on spawn's own surplus aggregate, not a debt-proportional one.
